groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

options.text: Prices rose, people bought less.
Prices rose, so people bought less.
Prices rose so, people bought less.

questions.explanation: Join two clauses with a conjunction (so), not just a comma.

options.text: Because the rent was too high.
They moved because the rent was too high.
The rent was too high.
The plan was expensive; however, it was approved.
The plan was expensive, however it was approved.
The plan was expensive however, it was approved.

questions.explanation: Semicolon before mid-sentence 'however', comma after it.

options.text: There are three reasons: cost, time and safety.
There are three reasons; cost, time and safety.
There are three reasons, cost: time and safety.
Students who study abroad gain confidence.
My sister, who studies abroad, is confident.
However, studying abroad is expensive.

questions.prompt: Correct the comma splice: 'Cities are growing, housing is scarce.'

options.text: Cities are growing, and housing is scarce.
Cities are growing housing is scarce.
Cities are growing, housing, is scarce.
Although it rained, the match continued.
Although it rained the match, continued.
Although, it rained the match continued.
He argued, that taxes should rise.
He argued that taxes should rise.
He argued that, taxes should rise.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a run-on (no punctuation between clauses)?

options.text: Fees rose students protested.
Fees rose, and students protested.
When fees rose, students protested.

questions.explanation: Two clauses with no linker or punctuation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best punctuation: 'Two factors matter most ___ price and location.'
